about: Refractive indices over temperature from published models fitted to measurements. CHARMS: absolute indices measured with the Cryogenic High-Accuracy Refraction Measuring System at NASA Goddard, as the published three-term Sellmeier models (model sellmeier) whose strengths S_i and wavelengths lambda_i (um) are 4th-order polynomials in the temperature in kelvin: n^2 - 1 = sum S_i(T) lambda^2 / (lambda^2 - lambda_i(T)^2), S_i(T) = sum_j S_ij T^j. JPCRD: the recommended indices of H. H. Li's critical reviews in the Journal of Physical and Chemical Reference Data, relative to air, which the module takes as dry air at 20 C and 1 atm. Germanium (model li-germanium): n^2 = epsilon(T) + exp(-3 dL/L293) (A0 + A1 T + A2 T^2) / lambda^2, with dL/L293 the lattice expansion from 293 K as two cubics meeting at 293 K, the lower one in (T - 100 K). The paper prints the lower cubic's constant as -0.089, a value in percent; as a fraction it is -8.9E-4, which makes the cubic vanish at 293 K and join the upper one with the same slope. ZnS and ZnSe (model li-zinc): n^2 = E(t) + A(t)/(lambda^2 - lambdaU(t)^2) + B(t)/(lambda^2/lambdaI(t)^2 - 1), t = T - 293 K. Coefficients are listed constant term first. Each material's expansion coefficient, cte, 1/K, is from the source it names.
